newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firm in active trade, diesel perks up.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firm in active trade, diesel perks up.

text.p: Strong German heating oil demand gave firm support to premiums and triggered active trade on Wednesday and low sulphur diesel buying revived as French suppliers sought to rebuild stocks, traders said.
Jan IPE gas oil ended up 75 cents at $230.25 a tonne and Feb IPE ended down 25 cents at $226 after NYMEX products recovered opening losses on cold European weather.

A 10,000 tonne cargo of German winter grade heating oil traded at Feb IPE +$9.25 for January 10-20 cif NWE. A 20,000 tonne cargo of low sulphur diesel traded at cif high quotes +$1 basis Bordeaux. Russian low sulphur diesel traded very prompt into NWE at Jan IPE +$6.

Traders said a 35,000 tonne cargo of low sulphur diesel was headed into NWE from Come by Chance refinery in Newfoundland, while a U.S. trader has taken a tanker for gas oil from the U.S. Gulf but has yet to determine specifications or destination.
Low sulphur diesel traded into Bordeaux at cif high quotes +$1/1.25 for January 24-30. French grade heating oil was unchanged at around Feb +$7/8.
Heating oil barges traded at Jan IPE +$3 fob ARA. Some parcels went a cif basis inland equivalent to +$4/5 fob ARA.
